paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when the pressure's on, David doesn't ask where the safest mountain is. He says, "In the LORD I take refuge." The advice he gets sounds practical, I'll give it that, and I'd have been hopping toward that mountain, gold base and all (Psalm 11:1). But David knows a hiding place only helps if it's bigger than the trouble, and no mountain is bigger than the LORD.

Why can David stay put? Because of where he says the LORD is: "The LORD is in His holy temple; the LORD is on His heavenly throne." Then he adds, "His eyes are watching closely; they examine the sons of men" (Psalm 11:4). The foundations can shake, the arrows can fly from the shadows, and the throne doesn't move. Nothing sneaks past Him, and nothing is out of His reach.

And here's what I love, baker. The LORD tests the righteous and the wicked, and His soul hates the lover of violence, but the psalm doesn't end on the coals and the scorching wind. It ends on "For the LORD is righteous; He loves justice. The upright will see His face" (Psalm 11:5-7). So the question isn't whether a mountain is ever the right move, it's where your refuge is, and David's is the LORD, who is righteous and loves justice.
